To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose three implicit recommenders based on CIPs that provide competitive recommendation quality and that handle incremental updates incorporating newly consumed items.

we introduce a novel implicit recommender that is competitive with existing techniques, including one that incorporates explicit feedback, and that it is generic and can be instantiated with several techniques, including one using word embedding.
We introduce the consumed item pack (i.e., CIP) which enables linking users (or items).
In summary, our research is concerned with
three contributions: (i) a novel notion of consumed item packs, (ii) three recommenders that are competitive with the stateof-the-art, and (iii) an incremental update scheme.
a novel implicit recommender that can be used to improve the recommendation quality of the web.
the design and analysis of novel recommenders that exploit implicit feedback.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CIP-U is the best of the four recommenders, followed by DEEPCIP and then CIP-I and FISM.
CIP-U and CIP-I are the most efficient recommenders, while DEEPCIP provides the best recommendation quality.
CIP-U and DEEPCIP provide a recommendation quality comparable to that of the state-of-the-art recommenders, but CIP-I is outperformed by them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce the notion CIP, which enables to link (users or items) based on implicit feedback.
we propose a novel recommendation technique that is able to capture the consumption of items in a pack, which is an implicit feedback.
our recommenders are competitive in recommendation quality while being simple and efficient to use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CIP is a simple and effective way to link users (items) based on their consumption history.

the CIPs provide a novel and effective means to relate users or items based on their implicit consumption patterns, which can be used to recommend content in many different contexts, such as movies, books, news articles, and music.
implicit feedback can be exploited to provide recommendations that are competitive with those using explicit feedback.
